name: Bamboo
description: Fastest-growing plant: up to 91 cm/day. Underground rhizome network stores energy for years before synchronized mass flowering across entire species worldwide. Hollow cylindrical geometry achieves maximum strength-to-weight ratio.

core_attributes.pattern: explosive vertical growth, rhizome energy storage, synchronized mass flowering

scope.definition: Growth rate efficiency of bamboo — daily biomass accumulation per unit leaf area index relative to theoretical photosynthetic maximum for C3 plants under tropical conditions.

evidence.source: Kleinhenz & Midmore (2001) 'Aspects of bamboo agronomy', Advances in Agronomy 74:99-153; Yen (2016) bamboo carbon sequestration studies.
cross_domain_examples: Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis): 91 cm/day maximum elongation rate — fastest angiosperm growth recorded
carbon sequestration 1.5-5× faster than equivalent forest area — photosynthetic efficiency matched by growth sink
sugarcane: highest C4 photosynthetic efficiency among crops 0.93 — bamboo C3 system approaches via growth rate optimization

scope.falsifiability: If bamboo growth rate per unit leaf area is statistically indistinguishable from other tropical C3 grasses, the exceptional growth rate is a size/vascular effect, not photosynthetic efficiency.
scope.measurement_limits: Peak growth (91 cm/day) occurs during spring shoot emergence — bamboo depletes rhizome starch reserves, not photosynthesis, for rapid elongation. Photosynthetic efficiency peak occurs during culm maturation phase.
